title: Contradish Transition Contract
description: The output of contradish's automatic warranted-transition derivation engine (contradish/transition_derivation.py): given a baseline and a changed scenario, which named commitments are warranted to change, what the correct new content is, and how confident the derivation was. This is the ground-truth spec that decision_relevance.score_dependency_structure() and minimal_intervention_delta.score_minimal_delta() otherwise require a human to hand-author (justified_commitments / invariant_commitments, a DistinctionPair's commit_a/commit_b). Published standalone, the same reasoning as distinction_report.schema.json: a transition contract produced by contradish's own engine, by a different implementation, or by a human working from the same rubric should all be comparable as this one shape -- which is exactly what an inter-implementation agreement study needs.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the payload was written against, as "<major>.<minor>". A minor bump only ever adds an optional field; a major bump is the only kind allowed to remove or repurpose one.

pair_id.description: Identifier of the scenario pair this contract was derived for.

domain.description: Name of the governing domain the scenario pair belongs to, e.g. "medication" or "immigration".

derived_by.description: Who or what produced this contract, e.g. "llm:LLMClient" or "manual:reviewer" -- lets two independently produced contracts for the same pair_id be told apart when comparing them.

commitments.description: One or more derived commitments for this scenario pair.

commitment_id.description: Name of the commitment this judgment is about.

warranted.description: true: the changed scenario's correct answer must differ from the baseline's (this case belongs in CW, the 'warranted a change' set). false: the correct answer should stay the same -- nothing here licenses a difference. null: genuinely undetermined, not guessed.

expected_effect.description: Free text describing what the changed scenario's correct answer should assert, when warranted is true. Empty when warranted is false or null. Same convention as DRSFactor.expected_effect elsewhere in contradish.

confidence.description: The deriver's own confidence in this judgment, 0.0-1.0.

rationale.description: One or two sentences on what specific new fact or circumstance, if any, makes this warranted or not.
